Looking at the error, `via` isn't a recognized argument on an `edge` line. Per the skeleton doc, explicit routing coordinates belong to the **layout zone**, where `pin` is the only directive — geometry that stabilises rendering but carries no meaning of its own. So the edge itself just states `probe -> normalizer` (the meaning), and the waypoints are pinned separately in the `layout` section, referencing that same edge and using the comma-separated multi-value convention (`class=hot,legacy`) applied to points.

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 block
title "Alert-forwarding chain"

node probe "Probe"
node normalizer "Normalizer"
node sink "Sink"

edge probe -> normalizer
edge normalizer -> sink

layout
pin probe->normalizer at=(60,20),(90,40)
```

Notes on the fix:

- Removed `via (60,20) (90,40)` from the `edge` line — that keyword doesn't parse there; the block genre keeps edge declarations meaning-only (source, target, optional label/class), never geometry.
- Added a `layout` zone with `pin probe->normalizer at=(60,20),(90,40)`, using the same `id -> id` reference as the edge declaration, and the language's existing comma-separated multi-value convention for the two waypoints.
- Everything else — the three nodes, both edges, the title — is unchanged from the prior attempt; nothing declared was weakened or dropped to make this parse.

Please run `node <skill-dir>/build-svg.js X.fd` on this — I can't execute the validator myself in this exchange, and if `pin`'s exact point-list grammar in `reference/layout.md` differs from the `at=(x,y),(x,y)` form assumed here, that's the one spot to check first.
